name: Streaming grid
description: World streaming's test scene (p353): a 1 km square cut into 16 × 16 cells of 64 m at rings 1 / 2 / 5. Each cell is code content: a procedural terrain block kept from FAR in (its ground, with a coarse LOD level), scattered rocks whose FAR stand-in is one InstancedMesh of an octahedral impostor, and crates (near only). And JSON content the gather cuts into cells: a beacon in every fourth cell, whose LOD levels give a FAR cell their coarsest level as far groups; a six-piece ruin of a small kit (a block, a slab and a post in two materials) in every cell with odd x and z, merged AUTO in 32 m cells while near and drawn far as its cell's far groups, each piece its own far entry (p377); and a 320 m wall across six cells, one entity kept while any of them is loaded. The camera flies across it and the cells around it load, switch between their near and far content and unload, fading in and out; the scene's debug tab switches to hovering on a cell boundary, and the Streaming tab's overlay shows the cells' states.

debugData.description: The main camera, so the streaming focus: streamingGrid.ts flies it across the grid (or hovers it on a cell boundary). Watch from the debug camera to see the cells load around it.
